passages.text: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
passages.sermon: Jacob was a man chosen by God.\r\nJacob began to travel on his journey.\r\nThe angels of God met Jacob on his way.
passages.original: וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב הָלַ֣ךְ לְדַרְכּ֑וֹ וַיִּפְגְּעוּ־ ב֖וֹ מַלְאֲכֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.
passages.sermon:
Jacob saw the angels of God.
Jacob spoke when he saw them.
Jacob said, “This is the camp of God.”
Jacob gave the place a name.
Jacob called the place Mahanaim.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאָ֔ם מַחֲנֵ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים זֶ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם־ הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מַֽחֲנָֽיִם׃פ

passages.text: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was traveling.
Jacob had a brother named Esau.
Esau lived in the land of Seir.
Seir was in the country of Edom.
Jacob sent messengers ahead of him.
Jacob sent these messengers to Esau.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֤ב מַלְאָכִים֙ לְפָנָ֔יו אֶל־ עֵשָׂ֖ו אָחִ֑יו אַ֥רְצָה שֵׂעִ֖יר שְׂדֵ֥ה אֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: He instructed them, “You are to say to my master Esau, ‘Your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to his messengers.
Jacob gave them instructions.
Jacob told them what to say to Esau.
Jacob called Esau “my master.”
Jacob called himself “your servant.”
Jacob said, “I have lived with Laban.”
Jacob said, “I have stayed there until now.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֤ו אֹתָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֔וּן לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לְעֵשָׂ֑ו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ עַבְדְּךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב עִם־ לָבָ֣ן גַּ֔רְתִּי וָאֵחַ֖ר עַד־ עָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants, and maidservants. I have sent this message to inform my master, so that I may find favor in your sight.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Esau.
Jacob said, “I have oxen.
I have donkeys.
I have flocks.
I have male servants.
I have female servants.
I sent this message to you, my master.
I want to find favor in your eyes.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי־ לִי֙ שׁ֣וֹר וַחֲמ֔וֹר צֹ֖אן וְעֶ֣בֶד וְשִׁפְחָ֑ה וָֽאֶשְׁלְחָה֙ לְהַגִּ֣יד לַֽאדֹנִ֔י לִמְצֹא־ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you—he and four hundred men with him.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob sent messengers to Esau, his brother.
The messengers returned to Jacob.
They spoke to Jacob.
They said, “We went to your brother Esau.
Esau is coming to meet you.
Four hundred men are with Esau.”
passages.original: וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּ֤אנוּ אֶל־ אָחִ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־ עֵשָׂ֔ו וְגַם֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ לִקְרָֽאתְךָ֔ וְאַרְבַּע־ מֵא֥וֹת אִ֖ישׁ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In great fear and distress, Jacob divided his people into two camps, as well as the flocks and herds and camels.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was very afraid.
Jacob felt great distress.
Jacob had many people with him.
Jacob also had flocks, herds, and camels.
Jacob divided the people into two groups.
Jacob divided the flocks, herds, and camels into two groups.
passages.original: וַיִּירָ֧א יַעֲקֹ֛ב מְאֹ֖ד וַיֵּ֣צֶר ל֑וֹ וַיַּ֜חַץ אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֗וֹ וְאֶת־ הַצֹּ֧אן וְאֶת־ הַבָּקָ֛ר וְהַגְּמַלִּ֖ים לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He thought, “If Esau comes and attacks one camp, then the other camp can escape.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was afraid of Esau.
Jacob had divided his people and animals into two camps.
Jacob thought about what might happen.
Jacob said, “If Esau comes to one camp and attacks it, that camp will be struck.”
Jacob said, “The other camp will be able to escape.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אִם־ יָב֥וֹא עֵשָׂ֛ו אֶל־ הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הָאַחַ֖ת וְהִכָּ֑הוּ וְהָיָ֛ה הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַנִּשְׁאָ֖ר לִפְלֵיטָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Jacob declared, “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, the LORD who told me, ‘Go back to your country and to your kindred, and I will make you prosper,’ I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to God.
Jacob called God the God of his father Abraham.
Jacob called God the God of his father Isaac.
Jacob spoke to the LORD.
The LORD had told Jacob, “Return to your country and to your family.
I will do good to you.”
Jacob said he was not worthy of all the kindness God had shown him.
Jacob said he was not worthy of all the faithfulness God had shown him.
Jacob said God had done these things for His servant.
Jacob said, “I crossed the Jordan River with only my staff.”
Jacob said, “Now I have become two camps.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ יַעֲקֹב֒ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אָבִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם וֵאלֹהֵ֖י אָבִ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק יְהוָ֞ה הָאֹמֵ֣ר אֵלַ֗י שׁ֧וּב לְאַרְצְךָ֛ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵיטִ֥יבָה עִמָּֽךְ׃ קָטֹ֜נְתִּי מִכֹּ֤ל הַחֲסָדִים֙ וּמִכָּל־ הָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֣י בְמַקְלִ֗י עָבַ֙רְתִּי֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה וְעַתָּ֥ה הָיִ֖יתִי לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid that he may come and attack me and the mothers and children with me.
passages.sermon:
Jacob prayed to God.
Jacob asked God to save him.
Jacob said, "Please deliver me from my brother Esau."
Jacob was afraid of Esau.
Jacob feared Esau might come and attack him.
Jacob was afraid Esau would hurt the mothers and the children with him.
passages.original: הַצִּילֵ֥נִי נָ֛א מִיַּ֥ד אָחִ֖י מִיַּ֣ד עֵשָׂ֑ו כִּֽי־ יָרֵ֤א אָנֹכִי֙ אֹת֔וֹ פֶּן־ יָב֣וֹא וְהִכַּ֔נִי אֵ֖ם עַל־ בָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jacob.
God promised to do good to Jacob.
God said He would make Jacob prosper.
God said He would make Jacob’s descendants very many.
God said Jacob’s offspring would be like the sand by the sea.
No one can count the sand by the sea.
No one will be able to count Jacob’s descendants because they will be so many.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֔רְתָּ הֵיטֵ֥ב אֵיטִ֖יב עִמָּ֑ךְ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י אֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams, 30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was afraid of his brother Esau.
Jacob stayed there that night.
Jacob had many animals with him.
Jacob chose a gift for Esau from what he had.
Jacob selected 200 female goats.
Jacob selected 20 male goats.
Jacob selected 200 ewes.
Jacob selected 20 rams.
Jacob selected 30 milk camels with their young.
Jacob selected 40 cows.
Jacob selected 10 bulls.
Jacob selected 20 female donkeys.
Jacob selected 10 male donkeys.
Jacob prepared all these animals as a gift for his brother Esau.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥לֶן שָׁ֖ם בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִן־ הַבָּ֧א בְיָד֛וֹ מִנְחָ֖ה לְעֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיו׃ עִזִּ֣ים מָאתַ֔יִם וּתְיָשִׁ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֑ים רְחֵלִ֥ים מָאתַ֖יִם וְאֵילִ֥ים עֶשְׂרִֽים׃ גְּמַלִּ֧ים מֵינִיק֛וֹת וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשִׁ֑ים פָּר֤וֹת אַרְבָּעִים֙ וּפָרִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֔ה אֲתֹנֹ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וַעְיָרִ֖ם עֲשָׂרָֽה׃

passages.text: He entrusted them to his servants in separate herds and told them, “Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob had many animals with him.
Jacob chose some animals as a gift for his brother Esau.
Jacob divided the animals into separate herds.
Jacob gave each herd to his servants.
Jacob spoke to his servants.
Jacob said, "Go ahead of me."
Jacob told them to keep space between each herd.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּן֙ בְּיַד־ עֲבָדָ֔יו עֵ֥דֶר עֵ֖דֶר לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַ֤יֹּאמֶר אֶל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ עִבְר֣וּ לְפָנַ֔י וְרֶ֣וַח תָּשִׂ֔ימוּ בֵּ֥ין עֵ֖דֶר וּבֵ֥ין עֵֽדֶר׃

passages.text: He instructed the one in the lead, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose animals are these before you?’
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the brother of Esau.
Jacob gave instructions to the servant who led the first group of animals.
Jacob said, "My brother Esau may meet you."
Esau may ask you questions.
Esau may say, 'Who do you belong to?'
Esau may say, 'Where are you going?'
Esau may say, 'Whose animals are these in front of you?'
Jacob told the servant to be ready for these questions.
passages.original: וַיְצַ֥ו אֶת־ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּ֣י יִֽפְגָּשְׁךָ֞ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֗י וִשְׁאֵֽלְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְמִי־ אַ֙תָּה֙ וְאָ֣נָה תֵלֵ֔ךְ וּלְמִ֖י אֵ֥לֶּה לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And behold, Jacob is behind us.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the owner of the animals.
Jacob was the brother of Esau.
Jacob sent the animals as a gift.
Jacob sent the gift to Esau.
Jacob called himself Esau’s servant.
Jacob told his servants to say this to Esau.
The animals belong to your servant Jacob.
They are a gift sent to my lord Esau.
Jacob is coming behind us.
passages.original: וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לְעַבְדְּךָ֣ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב מִנְחָ֥ה הִוא֙ שְׁלוּחָ֔ה לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לְעֵשָׂ֑ו וְהִנֵּ֥ה גַם־ ה֖וּא אַחֲרֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: He also instructed the second, the third, and all those following behind the herds: “When you meet Esau, you are to say the same thing to him.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the leader of his family and servants.
Jacob gave instructions to his messengers.
He spoke to the second messenger.
He spoke to the third messenger.
He spoke to everyone walking behind the herds.
Jacob told them what to say.
He said, “When you meet Esau, say the same words I told the first messenger.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֞ו גַּ֣ם אֶת־ הַשֵּׁנִ֗י גַּ֚ם אֶת־ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י גַּ֚ם אֶת־ כָּל־ הַהֹ֣לְכִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֥י הָעֲדָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ תְּדַבְּר֣וּן אֶל־ עֵשָׂ֔ו בְּמֹצַאֲכֶ֖ם אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You are also to say, ‘Look, your servant Jacob is right behind us.’ ” For he thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the servant of Esau.
Jacob sent a gift ahead to Esau.
Jacob told his messengers to say, “Look, your servant Jacob is right behind us.”
Jacob thought, “I will try to calm Esau with the gift that goes before me.”
After the gift, I will see Esau’s face.
Maybe Esau will accept me.”
passages.original: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם גַּ֗ם הִנֵּ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אַחֲרֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־ אָמַ֞ר אֲכַפְּרָ֣ה פָנָ֗יו בַּמִּנְחָה֙ הַהֹלֶ֣כֶת לְפָנָ֔י וְאַחֲרֵי־ כֵן֙ אֶרְאֶ֣ה פָנָ֔יו אוּלַ֖י יִשָּׂ֥א פָנָֽי׃

passages.text: So Jacob’s gifts went on before him, while he spent the night in the camp.
passages.sermon:
Jacob sent his gifts ahead of him.
The gifts passed in front of Jacob.
Jacob stayed in the camp that night.
He spent the night there.
passages.original: וַתַּעֲבֹ֥ר הַמִּנְחָ֖ה עַל־ פָּנָ֑יו וְה֛וּא לָ֥ן בַּלַּֽיְלָה־ הַה֖וּא בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a servant of God.
Jacob had two wives.
Jacob had two maidservants.
Jacob had eleven sons.
It was night.
Jacob got up during the night.
Jacob took his two wives.
Jacob took his two maidservants.
Jacob took his eleven sons.
Jacob led them all.
Jacob crossed the ford of the Jabbok with them.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם׀ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה ה֗וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־ שְׁתֵּ֤י נָשָׁיו֙ וְאֶת־ שְׁתֵּ֣י שִׁפְחֹתָ֔יו וְאֶת־ אַחַ֥ד עָשָׂ֖ר יְלָדָ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔ר אֵ֖ת מַעֲבַ֥ר יַבֹּֽק׃

passages.text: He took them and sent them across the stream, along with all his possessions.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a patriarch of Israel.
Jacob had two wives, two maidservants, and eleven sons.
Jacob also had many possessions.
Jacob took his wives, maidservants, and sons.
Jacob sent them across the stream.
Jacob sent all his possessions across the stream.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּחֵ֔ם וַיַּֽעֲבִרֵ֖ם אֶת־ הַנָּ֑חַל וַֽיַּעֲבֵ֖ר אֶת־ אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ׃

passages.text: So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was alone.
A man came to Jacob.
The man wrestled with Jacob.
They wrestled until the sun began to rise.
passages.original: וַיִּוָּתֵ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַיֵּאָבֵ֥ק אִישׁ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ עַ֖ד עֲל֥וֹת הַשָּֽׁחַר׃

passages.text: When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.
passages.sermon:
A man wrestled with Jacob.
The man saw that he could not defeat Jacob.
The man touched the socket of Jacob’s hip.
Jacob’s hip was dislocated while they wrestled.
passages.original: וַיַּ֗רְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָכֹל֙ ל֔וֹ וַיִּגַּ֖ע בְּכַף־ יְרֵכ֑וֹ וַתֵּ֙קַע֙ כַּף־ יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּהֵֽאָבְק֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the man said, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” But Jacob replied, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was alone at night.
A man wrestled with Jacob until daybreak.
The man spoke to Jacob.
The man said, "Let me go. It is daybreak."
Jacob answered the man.
Jacob said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שַׁלְּחֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י עָלָ֖ה הַשָּׁ֑חַר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲשַֽׁלֵּחֲךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם־ בֵּרַכְתָּֽנִי׃

passages.text: “What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
A man wrestled with Jacob.
The man spoke to Jacob.
The man asked Jacob a question.
The man said, “What is your name?”
Jacob answered the man.
Jacob said, “Jacob.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו מַה־ שְּׁמֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Jacob.
The man said, “Your name will not be Jacob anymore.
Your name will be Israel.
You have struggled with God.
You have struggled with men.
You have prevailed.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ שָׂרִ֧יתָ עִם־ אֱלֹהִ֛ים וְעִם־ אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַתּוּכָֽל׃

passages.text: And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.” But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed Jacob there.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke.
Jacob asked the man.
Jacob said, "Please tell me your name."
The man answered Jacob.
The man said, "Why do you ask my name?"
The man blessed Jacob there.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֣א שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה תִּשְׁאַ֣ל לִשְׁמִ֑י וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֹת֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob had just wrestled with a man who was God in human form.
Jacob named the place Peniel.
Peniel means "face of God."
Jacob said, "I have seen God face to face."
Jacob's life was spared.
Jacob survived after seeing God.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֧א יַעֲקֹ֛ב שֵׁ֥ם הַמָּק֖וֹם פְּנִיאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ רָאִ֤יתִי אֱלֹהִים֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל־ פָּנִ֔ים וַתִּנָּצֵ֖ל נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a patriarch of Israel.
Jacob passed by a place called Penuel.
The sun rose above Jacob as he went by.
Jacob was limping.
His limp was because of his hip.
passages.original: וַיִּֽזְרַֽח־ ל֣וֹ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָבַ֖ר אֶת־ פְּנוּאֵ֑ל וְה֥וּא צֹלֵ֖עַ עַל־ יְרֵכֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon which is at the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are God's chosen people.
They do not eat the tendon that is at the socket of the hip.
They have kept this practice until today.
They do this because God struck Jacob’s hip at that tendon.
Jacob’s hip was touched during his encounter with God.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־ יֹאכְל֨וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ גִּ֣יד הַנָּשֶׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ כַּ֣ף הַיָּרֵ֔ךְ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י נָגַע֙ בְּכַף־ יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּגִ֖יד הַנָּשֶֽׁה׃
